title: Service-class fairshare admission controller for tiered lanes (free/paid/enterprise)
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Implement an admission controller that enforces quota-aware prioritization across service classes (free, paid, enterprise) while enabling graceful degradation and model-variant fallbacks. The controller should: 1) enforce per-tenant and per-lane soft-reserves, 2) adapt weights dynamically based on remaining quota and recent latency compliance, 3) allow regional spillover where enterprise contracts permit, and 4) select a fallback model variant when the preferred model is unavailable or quota-constrained (e.g., compressed/quantized variant for free lane).
acceptance_criteria: Tiered routing decision executed within <= 5ms median per-request in staging
Respect soft-reserve: enterprise lane maintains configured minimal throughput during overload
Free lane may be demoted to quantized fallback without violating error-rate SLOs
Automated telemetry exposes per-lane drop rates, average admission latency, and quota burn rates
Canary rollout to 10% of traffic and rollback if 99th percentile latency regresses >10%
design_decisions: Use multi-queue token-bucket admission: one queue per service class + shared overflow queue
Weights computed from (remaining_quota_ratio * configured_priority_weight) and smoothed with exponential decay (alpha=0.25)
Soft-reserve semantics: each enterprise tenant receives a minimum reservation computed from commit / reserved capacity; paid tenants get a smaller soft reserve; free gets no guaranteed reserve
Fallback model selection: maintain compatibility map per-model that lists lighter/quantized variants; fallbacks subject to latency and quality thresholds
Regional spillover enabled by default only for enterprise tier; paid tier requires opt-in; free tier always local-only
Admission decisions are stateless per-request but consult a fast in-memory quota cache updated from central quota service asynchronously every 250ms
rollout_plan: 2) Unit tests and integration tests in CI for admission logic and fallback choosing
3) Deploy to staging with synthetic load (tiered mixes) and validate telemetry
4) Canary: route 1% -> 5% -> 10% traffic over 24-hour windows; monitor SLOs and cost impact
5) Gradual enable for paid customers, opt-in for paid/enterprise during first month, then global enable for free after metrics stable
6) Rollback plan: toggle feature flag off; circuit-break to default simple-tier-router if severe regressions
test_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket logic, weight computation, and fallback mapping
End-to-end integration tests with quota service stub simulating quota exhaustion and replenishment
Load test matrix: (free-heavy, paid-heavy, enterprise-heavy) mixes at 0.5x,1x,2x expected traffic
Chaos test: simulate regional outage and verify spillover respects tenant permissions
Quality regression: verify BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity thresholds for fallback model variants on representative prompt set
